feedback: [check 5] Legibility: At 1440px, <a.block.paper2 > div.bmeta > span.yr> "2026" at 14px over div.halftone (positioned background-image): #96691f is under 4.5:1 across 100% of one pixel row through its glyphs (4.00:1 on #f0e9d8). Give the text a flat ground that clears the ratio (a background on its own box), or stop the lines, image or layer behind it short of the text.

1. (Judgment 5) The Spaceman block says "A tracking layer for the things that drift — built to be read at a glance and trusted at 3am, where the hard part was never the data but deciding what deserved the screen." The record describes Spaceman as the LLC Doug has run since 2018 for independent product design, frontend engineering, design systems and brand work with clients such as Rolex, Intuit and LastPass. Replace the line with copy drawn from that record.

2. (Judgment 1) Tonight reads as a rerun of 2026-10-21. That night was also a full-bleed, crowded work-index specimen led by the list, in hue 46 gold, with halftone ground and small-caps/roman/justified/stacked type. Tonight repeats the hue, the material, the whole type register and the silhouette. Change at least the ground material and the type register (case, alignment or texture) so a returning visitor would not take it for that night.

3. (Judgment 2) At 1440 the justified standfirst "Deep in both. Not a generalist." spreads six words across the full band with gaps of roughly 100px or more. It reads as scattered words, not one line. Set it so the words hold together as a phrase across the band, for example with tracking, a larger step within the standfirst rank, or a constrained measure that is still justified.

1. (Judgment 1) This reads as a rerun of 2026-10-21, the "foundry specimen of the work": the same 46° gold, the same small-caps/roman/justified/stacked display register, the same full-bleed crowded list-led index of stacked project titles, and the same halftone ground. Change at least two of these, for example a different case/texture register for the titles and a hue or ground that does not read as gold-on-dark, so a returning visitor does not mistake it for that night.
2. (Judgment 6) SHELL `ground_material: halftone` is not on the hero field. The umber masthead and the index blocks carry evenly spaced horizontal ruled lines, which reads as notebook rule, not halftone dots. Replace the rules with a halftone screen on the masthead field.
3. (Judgment 3) Type Treatment `alignment: justified` is not executed on the standfirst. "Deep in both. Not a generalist." sits left-set and short, filling about a third of the band at 1440. Justify it edge to edge across the full-bleed masthead as declared.

1. Freshness: this reads as a rerun of 2026-10-21, "a foundry specimen of the work, the maxim inscribed in gold." Both nights share these traits:
- the same 46° gold
- halftone dots on a dark field
- a crowded full-bleed list hero
- condensed small-caps display titles, roman, justified and stacked (Big Shoulders here, Bebas there)
- a standfirst band over a packed index of the same project titles

Break at least two of these. Move the accent well off 46° gold, or make the paper ground carry the page instead of the dark umber with brass blocks. Then change the type register: drop small-caps, or drop the stacked condensed signage set.

2. Legibility, 1440 masthead: the standfirst "Deep in both. Not a generalist." is justified across a single line. The word gaps are wider than the words themselves, so the phrase reads as six scattered labels, not a sentence. Keep `alignment: justified` but give it a real measure. Either break it into two justified lines ("Deep in both." / "Not a generalist.") or bound the band so the gaps close to normal word spacing.

3. Hierarchy: the declared lead is the first project title, SPACEMAN. At 1440 it renders at the same size as FISHSTICKS and 15TH CLUB, and it sits on dark umber while FISHSTICKS sits on a bright brass block. The bright block wins the eye. Make the featured Spaceman block lead the index: give it a larger span, the brass ground, or a step up in size, so the eye lands on it first and then accelerates through the rest.
